anchorData: SOUND: speed of sound in air near Nairobi = 340 m/s (use 340 everywhere). Matatu horn true frequency f = 400 Hz, so wavelength = 340/400 = 0.85 m. Music in the matatu spans 200 Hz to 1000 Hz: 200 Hz gives 1.7 m, 1000 Hz gives 0.34 m. Matatu speed = 15 m/s (= 54 km/h). DOPPLER (matatu): approaching f' = 400x340/(340-15) = 400x340/325 = 418 Hz; receding f' = 400x340/(340+15) = 400x340/355 = 383 Hz; the pitch drop is 418-383 = 35 Hz. Ambulance siren: 700 Hz at 20 m/s gives 700x340/320 = 744 Hz approaching and 700x340/360 = 661 Hz receding. CORNER: street opening the sound passes through/around = 4.0 m wide. 400 Hz: wavelength/gap = 0.85/4.0 = 0.21 (clearly bends). Visible light wavelength = 500 nm = 5.0x10^-7 m (ratio to 4.0 m gap about 1.3x10^-7, essentially no bending). LIGHT: speed in air = 3.0x10^8 m/s. RIPPLE TANK: vibrator frequency 10 Hz in both depths. Deep water: v = 0.30 m/s, wavelength = 3.0 cm. Shallow water: v = 0.20 m/s, wavelength = 2.0 cm (frequency stays 10 Hz). REFLECTION: echo test, student claps 85 m from a wall; echo returns after 2x85/340 = 0.50 s. Minimum distance for a separate echo (0.10 s delay) = 340x0.10/2 = 17 m. SONAR on Lake Victoria: speed of sound in water = 1500 m/s; pulse returns after 0.040 s; depth = 1500x0.040/2 = 30 m. REFRACTION: light air to water, refractive index of water = 1.33; incident angle 40 degrees gives refracted angle about 29 degrees (sin r = sin40/1.33 = 0.643/1.33 = 0.483); speed of light in water = 3.0x10^8/1.33 = 2.26x10^8 m/s. INTERFERENCE: two speakers both play 340 Hz so wavelength = 1.00 m; path difference 1.00 m gives a loud spot (constructive); path difference 0.50 m gives a quiet spot (destructive). FM radio station frequency = 100 MHz = 1.0x10^8 Hz; wavelength = 3.0x10^8/1.0x10^8 = 3.0 m. Near the Ngong Hills the signal arriving directly and the signal reflected off the hillside overlap; weak spots are half a wavelength apart = 1.5 m. STANDING WAVES: guitar string length L = 0.65 m, wave speed on string 143 m/s; fundamental wavelength = 2L = 1.30 m; f = 143/1.30 = 110 Hz (2 nodes at the ends, 1 antinode). Second harmonic: wavelength 0.65 m, f = 220 Hz (3 nodes, 2 antinodes). Pressing the string to a length of 0.325 m (same tension) gives wavelength 0.65 m and f = 220 Hz (higher note from shorter string). ULTRASOUND: medical frequency 3.5 MHz = 3.5x10^6 Hz; speed in soft tissue 1540 m/s; wavelength = 1540/3.5x10^6 = 4.4x10^-4 m = 0.44 mm. FM MODULATION: carrier 100 MHz; a 1 kHz audio tone changes the carrier frequency (frequency deviation up to 75 kHz) while amplitude stays constant.
characters: Mr Kamau: Physics teacher at a Nairobi secondary school who leads the investigations. Wanjiru and Otieno: Grade 10 students who stand around the corner of a building on a busy Nairobi street and hear the music but cannot see the matatu. Baraka: the matatu driver on the Nairobi-Ngong route; he keeps the horn steady at 400 Hz and never changes it. The matatu: speeds at a constant 15 m/s, has a horn at 400 Hz and a radio tuned to a 100 MHz FM station that never changes. The building: a concrete wall hiding the parked matatu; the street opening around it is 4.0 m wide. Ngong Hills: hillside south-west of Nairobi that reflects radio signals, creating fading spots about 1.5 m apart. Lake Victoria (Kisumu): where fishers use sonar fish-finders; depth example 30 m. Classroom: has a ripple tank, two speakers, a slinky, a guitar string and a small buzzer on a string.
outcome: The music is heard around the building because sound waves of wavelength 0.34 m to 1.7 m are comparable to the 4.0 m opening and diffract (bend) around the corner, while light of wavelength 5.0x10^-7 m hardly diffracts at all, so the torch beam is blocked. The horn sounds 418 Hz while the matatu approaches and 383 Hz while it recedes, because the moving source compresses the waves ahead of it and stretches them behind it (Doppler effect), although the horn really stays at 400 Hz. The FM signal fades at certain spots near the Ngong Hills because the direct signal and the signal reflected from the hillside interfere, cancelling where they meet in destructive interference (about 1.5 m apart) and reinforcing again between those spots; the station itself never changes.
conventions: Use 'wavelength' with symbol lambda (written λ) in metres; frequency f in hertz (Hz); wave speed v in m/s; period T = 1/f. The wave equation is always called 'the wave equation v = fλ'. Use 340 m/s for sound in air, 3.0x10^8 m/s for light in air. Say 'pitch' for what we hear related to frequency, and 'loudness' for amplitude. A wavefront is a line joining points in phase; rays are drawn perpendicular to wavefronts. Angles are measured from the normal. Law of reflection: angle of incidence i = angle of reflection r. Refraction: frequency does not change, speed and wavelength change; refractive index n = c/v = sin i / sin r. Diffraction is the spreading of waves around an obstacle or through a gap, greatest when wavelength is comparable to or bigger than the gap. Interference is the superposition of waves; constructive when path difference = nλ, destructive when path difference = (n+1/2)λ. Standing wave: nodes (no movement) and antinodes (maximum movement); string length L = λ/2 for the fundamental. Doppler formulas: approaching f' = f v/(v - vs); receding f' = f v/(v + vs). Round frequencies to the nearest Hz. Always write the fixed figures exactly as in anchorData. Use Kenyan contexts. Each lesson has 5 phases: Predict, Observe, Explain, DQB creation, Model building. The model is one class model with three parts: A (corner/diffraction), B (pitch/Doppler), C (signal fading/interference). Do not teach ideas assigned to other lessons; only refer back to earlier lessons.

lessonMap.focus: The matatu mystery: launching the phenomenon
lessonMap.teaches: Observing the three puzzles (sound heard around corner, pitch change, FM fading) and asking testable questions; initial models; what a wave is as a disturbance carrying energy
lessonMap.buildsOn: None; first lesson, uses only prior knowledge of sound and light
lessonMap.usesData: Matatu speed 15 m/s, horn 400 Hz, 418 Hz and 383 Hz heard (values only observed, not calculated), 100 MHz FM station, 4.0 m opening

lessonMap.teaches: Rectilinear propagation: waves travel in straight lines in a uniform medium; rays and wavefronts
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 1 questions about why the torch beam is blocked by the wall
lessonMap.usesData: Light speed 3.0x10^8 m/s, ripple tank 10 Hz, deep water wavelength 3.0 cm, v = 0.30 m/s

lessonMap.focus: Reflection and the laws of reflection
lessonMap.teaches: Law of reflection (i = r, incident ray, reflected ray and normal in the same plane) shown with plane mirrors and ripple barriers
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 2 rays and wavefronts; Lesson 1 model
lessonMap.usesData: Ripple tank 10 Hz, wavelength 3.0 cm; echo test 85 m, 0.50 s

lessonMap.focus: Applications of reflection: echoes, sonar, halls
lessonMap.teaches: Using reflection of sound with time delay to find distance (d = vt/2); echo minimum distance and hall acoustics
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 3 law of reflection; speed of sound from Lesson 1 data
lessonMap.usesData: Echo 0.50 s at 85 m, 17 m minimum distance, Lake Victoria sonar 1500 m/s, 0.040 s, 30 m

lessonMap.teaches: Refraction is a change of direction caused by a change of wave speed at a boundary; bending toward the normal when slowing
lessonMap.usesData: Ripple tank deep v = 0.30 m/s and shallow v = 0.20 m/s; light in air and water, 40 degrees to 29 degrees (observed qualitatively)

lessonMap.teaches: Using v = fλ and n = sin i / sin r: frequency stays constant while wavelength changes; explaining the bent straw
lessonMap.usesData: 10 Hz, 3.0 cm to 2.0 cm; n = 1.33, 40 degrees to 29 degrees, 2.26x10^8 m/s

lessonMap.teaches: Diffraction of waves through gaps and around edges, strongest when wavelength is comparable to or larger than the gap
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lessons 2 and 6 (straight-line travel, wavelength, v = fλ)
lessonMap.usesData: Ripple tank 3.0 cm wavelength with varying gap widths; matatu opening 4.0 m introduced as the real gap

lessonMap.teaches: Comparing sound and light wavelengths with the 4.0 m opening to explain why sound turns the corner and light does not; high pitches bend less than low pitches
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 7 diffraction rule; Lessons 1 and 2 questions on the torch beam
lessonMap.usesData: Wavelengths 0.85 m, 1.7 m, 0.34 m; light 5.0x10^-7 m; ratio 0.21; 4.0 m opening

lessonMap.teaches: Superposition and interference: constructive and destructive using path difference (nλ and (n+1/2)λ); loud and quiet spots; explains FM fading
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lessons 6 and 8 (wavelength, v = fλ, waves spreading from sources)
lessonMap.usesData: Speakers 340 Hz, wavelength 1.00 m, path differences 1.00 m and 0.50 m; FM 100 MHz, wavelength 3.0 m, fading spots 1.5 m apart

lessonMap.teaches: Standing waves from superposition of waves travelling opposite ways: nodes, antinodes, L = λ/2, and how length and tension set the note
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 9 interference and superposition; Lesson 3 reflection at fixed ends
lessonMap.usesData: Guitar string 0.65 m, 143 m/s, 110 Hz, 220 Hz, 0.325 m; 1.5 m spacing of fading spots linked as half a wavelength

lessonMap.teaches: Apparent change in frequency due to relative motion of source and observer; use of f' = f v/(v - vs) and f' = f v/(v + vs)
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 6 (v = fλ, wavelength and frequency); Lesson 1 pitch observations
lessonMap.usesData: Horn 400 Hz, 15 m/s, 418 Hz, 383 Hz, 35 Hz drop; ambulance 700 Hz, 20 m/s, 744 Hz, 661 Hz
